newsitem.title: AFGHANISTAN: Floods kill 24 in northern Afghanistan.
newsitem.headline: Floods kill 24 in northern Afghanistan.

text.p: Recent flooding has killed 24 people and destroyed at least 600 houses and hundreds of acres of farmland in northern Afganistan, a spokeswoman for the United Nations said on Wednesday.

"Rivers in the (northern Afghan provinces of) Balkh, Jozjan and Faryab have burst their banks, destroying irrigation canals and flooding farmland," said U.N. spokeswoman Sarah Russell, speaking by telephone from the Pakistani capital Islamabad.
Russell said 12 bodies had been found in one river south of the northern provincial capital, Mazar-i-Sharif.

"A survey carried out by the U.N. and non-governmental organisations of the Balkh river reports that between (the villages of) Sholgara and Dowlatabad, 12 bodies were found in the river, more than 100 houses had been destroyed and 940 hectares (2,350 acres) of farmland eroded," she said.
"From other areas: another six dead, 500 houses destroyed, 26 grain mills washed away, 1,900 farm animals dead and hundreds of hectares of farmland under water," she said.
Russell said the survey reported more than 7,000 hectares (17,500 acres) of land had been affected, but total damage was expected to be much higher.
"The villages of Chinzai and Mongala have been cut off. A huge area has been affected and access is difficult," she said.
The floods are due to heavy rains over the past three weeks.
The main problems victims of the flooding face would be a shortage of food and clean water, according to Russell. Some aid agencies had already started aid distributions.

"Open wells in villages have collapsed or been flooded, creating drinking water problems. The main problems will be food and clean water. The International Committee of the Red Cross and the Afghan Red Crescent Society have distributed food and non-food items in Faryab province," she said.
"The U.N. World Food Programme says it has 500 tonnes of wheat standing by for this kind of event and will provide food immediately to Sholgara -- the area that has been worst hit.
"U.N. agencies and (the U.K.-based aid agency) Oxfam are to repair bridges and carry out engineering work to mend canals and restore water supplies," said Russell.
